417	def _merge_node(left: dict, right: dict) -> dict:
418	    """Fold two schema nodes over disjoint batches into one new node."""
419	    kind = left["kind"]
420	    if kind == "object":
421	        if _is_collapsed(left) or _is_collapsed(right):
422	            # One side gave up per-field detail, so the union can only be
423	            # reported as a collapsed, marked summary.
424	            node = _collapsed_node("object")
425	            node["count"] = left["count"] + right["count"]
426	            return node
427	        node = _new_node("object")
428	        node["count"] = left["count"] + right["count"]
429	        left_overflow = left.get("overflow")
430	        right_overflow = right.get("overflow")
431	        names = list(left["fields"]) + [
432	            name for name in right["fields"] if name not in left["fields"]
433	        ]
434	        for name in names:
435	            le = left["fields"].get(name)
436	            re = right["fields"].get(name)
437	            if le is None:
438	                # The field is missing on the left; if the left capped its
439	                # fields, its occurrences of this field landed in the left
440	                # overflow entry, so the merged entry must absorb them and
441	                # be marked approximate. That field's own occurrences on
442	                # the right prove its name is folded too.
443	                if left_overflow is not None:
444	                    entry = _merge_field(left_overflow, re)
445	                    _overflow_add_name(entry, name)
446	                    entry["approximate"] = True
447	                else:
448	                    entry = copy.deepcopy(re)
449	            elif re is None:
450	                if right_overflow is not None:
451	                    entry = _merge_field(le, right_overflow)
452	                    _overflow_add_name(entry, name)
453	                    entry["approximate"] = True
454	                else:
455	                    entry = copy.deepcopy(le)
456	            else:
457	                entry = _merge_field(le, re)
458	            node["fields"][name] = entry
459	        if left_overflow is not None or right_overflow is not None:
460	            if left_overflow is None:
461	                overflow = copy.deepcopy(right_overflow)
462	            elif right_overflow is None:
463	                overflow = copy.deepcopy(left_overflow)
464	            else:
465	                overflow = _merge_field(left_overflow, right_overflow)
466	            overflow["approximate"] = True
467	            node["overflow"] = overflow
468	        return node
469	    if kind == "array":
470	        node = _new_node("array")
471	        if left.get("approximate") or right.get("approximate"):
472	            node["approximate"] = True
473	        kinds = list(left["elements"]) + [
474	            element_kind
475	            for element_kind in right["elements"]

491	def _merge_field(left: dict, right: dict) -> dict:
492	    """Fold two field entries over disjoint batches into one new entry."""
493	    entry = _new_field()
494	    entry["observed"] = left["observed"] + right["observed"]
495	    if left.get("approximate") or right.get("approximate"):
496	        entry["approximate"] = True

498	    # to ordinary exact entries would make the merged tree differ from a
499	    # single one-shot fold over the same records.
500	    if "names" in left or "names" in right:
501	        entry["names"] = _union_overflow_names(left, right)

503	        kind for kind in right["types"] if kind not in left["types"]
504	    ]
505	    for kind in kinds:
506	        lc = left["types"].get(kind)
507	        rc = right["types"].get(kind)
508	        if lc is None:
509	            entry["types"][kind] = copy.deepcopy(rc)
510	        elif rc is None:
511	            entry["types"][kind] = copy.deepcopy(lc)
512	        else:
513	            entry["types"][kind] = _merge_node(lc, rc)

519	    kind = mem["kind"]
520	    if kind == "object":
521	        if _is_collapsed(mem):

528	        for name, entry in mem["fields"].items():
529	            base_entry = base_fields.get(name)
530	            if base_entry is None:

532	            else:
533	                node["fields"][name] = _subtract_field(entry, base_entry)
534	        mem_overflow = mem.get("overflow")
535	        if mem_overflow is not None:

537	            if base_overflow is None:
538	                node["overflow"] = copy.deepcopy(mem_overflow)
539	            else:
540	                node["overflow"] = _subtract_field(mem_overflow, base_overflow)

542	    if kind == "array":
543	        node = _new_node("array")

545	            node["approximate"] = True

547	        for element_kind, child in mem["elements"].items():
548	            base_child = base_elements.get(element_kind)
549	            if base_child is None:

551	            else:

557	def _subtract_field(mem: dict, base: dict) -> dict:
558	    entry = _new_field()
559	    entry["observed"] = mem["observed"] - base["observed"]
560	    if mem.get("approximate"):
561	        entry["approximate"] = True
562	    mem_names = mem.get("names")
563	    if mem_names is not None:
564	        # The delta cannot attribute provenance per name (only aggregate
565	        # counts are kept), so it carries every name its memory ever folded
566	        # in; the downstream merge is a union anyway, and over-inclusion
567	        # only ever widens validation for genuinely folded names.
568	        entry["names"] = sorted(mem_names)

570	        base_child = base["types"].get(kind)
571	        if base_child is None:
572	            entry["types"][kind] = copy.deepcopy(child)
573	        else:
574	            entry["types"][kind] = _subtract_node(child, base_child)

578	def _join(path: str, name: str) -> str:
579	    # An identifier is joined with a dot; every other key is quoted in
580	    # brackets so a name containing a dot or a backslash can never be read
581	    # as a path separator: $["a.b"] is distinct from $.a.b.
582	    if name.isidentifier():
583	        return f"{path}.{name}"
584	    return f"{path}[{json.dumps(name)}]"

587	def _marker_path(path: str) -> str:
588	    """Render the overflow-marker location beneath an object node.
589	
590	    The marker can never be a real key (see ``OVERFLOW_MARKER``), so a bare
591	    ``.*`` segment cannot be produced by ``_join`` for any real field name;
592	    a field literally named "*" quotes as ``$["*"]`` and stays distinct.
593	    """
594	    return f"{path}.*"

597	def _check_object(node: dict, record: dict, path: str, reports: list[str]) -> None:
598	    if _is_collapsed(node):
599	        # A depth-capped node tracked no fields, so nothing inside the
600	        # record's value can be checked; the approximation is marked in
601	        # the schema instead of guessed about here.
602	        return
603	    fields = node["fields"]
604	    overflow = node.get("overflow")
605	    overflow_names = None if overflow is None else overflow.get("names")
606	    for name in record:
607	        if name not in fields:
608	            if overflow is not None and (
609	                overflow_names is None or name in overflow_names
610	            ):
611	                # Only names that really folded into the overflow entry are
612	                # checked against its widened type set; ``names is None``
613	                # marks a legacy overflow entry with unknown provenance. A
614	                # name never seen before is still unexpected.
615	                _check_value(overflow["types"], record[name], _join(path, name), reports)
616	            else:
617	                reports.append(f"{_join(path, name)}: unexpected field")
618	    for name, entry in fields.items():
619	        if name not in record:
620	            if not entry["optional"]:
621	                reports.append(f"{_join(path, name)}: missing required field")
622	            continue
623	        _check_value(entry["types"], record[name], _join(path, name), reports)

626	def _check_value(types: dict, value: Any, path: str, reports: list[str]) -> None:
627	    kind = _kind_of(value)
628	    node = types.get(kind)
629	    if node is None:
630	        expected = ", ".join(sorted(types))
631	        reports.append(f"{path}: type {kind} not in field types [{expected}]")
632	        return
633	    if kind == "object":
634	        _check_object(node, value, path, reports)
635	    elif kind == "array":
636	        for index, element in enumerate(value):
637	            _check_value(node["elements"], element, f"{path}[{index}]", reports)

640	# -- cross-revision compatibility -------------------------------------------
641	#
642	# Compatibility is read straight off the two committed schema trees, using
643	# exactly what ``check`` decides with: a record is accepted when every
644	# field it carries is a known (or genuinely overflow-folded) field whose
645	# value kind is in the entry's type set, every required field is present,
646	# and nested branches recurse. One symmetric walk therefore derives both
647	# directions at once: ``backward`` asks whether the new tree accepts every
648	# record the old tree accepts, ``forward`` the reverse.
649	#
650	# Each branch returns a ``(backward, forward)`` verdict pair. A branch
651	# either tree can only describe approximately - an overflow entry that may
652	# route the field, an entry flagged approximate, or a depth-capped subtree
653	# - is unknown in both directions and lists its source, in the same paths
654	# ``stats`` uses for approximated statistics (``$.*`` for an overflow
655	# entry, the subtree's own path for a collapsed node). The one exception
656	# is comparing a revision with itself: that revision is known to accept its
657	# own records, so ``Lens.compat`` answers compatible in both directions
658	# with no reasons after the revision has been read and validated.
659	
660	_COMPATIBLE = "compatible"
661	_BREAKING = "breaking"
662	_UNKNOWN = "unknown"
663	
664	# Witness recipe step tags (see ``_CompatDiffer``): an object field
665	# descent, one array-element nesting, a forced-kind leaf, and an omission
666	# of the innermost field.
667	_FIELD = "f"
668	_ARRAY = "a"
669	_KIND = "k"
670	_MISSING = "m"
671	
672	
673	def _combine_pair(pair: tuple[str, str], other: tuple[str, str]) -> tuple[str, str]:
674	    return (_worst(pair[0], other[0]), _worst(pair[1], other[1]))
675	
676	
677	def _worst(left: str, right: str) -> str:
678	    """Aggregate branch verdicts for one direction.
679	
680	    A branch that demonstrably rejects a legal record settles the
681	    direction as breaking even when another branch is unknowable; without
682	    one of those an unknown branch degrades it to unknown.
683	    """
684	    if left == _BREAKING or right == _BREAKING:
685	        return _BREAKING
686	    if left == _UNKNOWN or right == _UNKNOWN:
687	        return _UNKNOWN
688	    return _COMPATIBLE

691	def _overflow_live(entry: dict) -> bool:
692	    """Whether an overflow entry can route a field name during check.
693	
694	    An entry with known but empty provenance routes nothing; an explicit
695	    ``names: None`` (a pre-tracking overflow entry) routes any name.
696	    """
697	    names = entry.get("names", [])
698	    return names is None or bool(names)
699	
700	
701	def _overflow_routes(entry: dict | None, name: str) -> bool:
702	    if entry is None or not _overflow_live(entry):
703	        return False
704	    names = entry.get("names")
705	    return names is None or name in names

708	class _CompatDiffer:
709	    """Symmetric diff of two validated snapshots, aligned with ``check``."""
710	
711	    def __init__(self) -> None:
712	        self.changes: list[dict] = []
713	        self.reasons: set[str] = set()
714	        # One deterministic witness recipe per breaking pair position. Each
715	        # recipe is a tuple of tagged steps from the root object to that
716	        # position, so a record can be built straight from a schema tree
717	        # without matching change strings, re-deriving the alignment, or
718	        # risking a collision between a real field name and a step token:
719	        # ``("f", name)`` descends through an object field, ``("a",)``
720	        # through one array element nesting, and the terminal step is
721	        # either ``("k", kind)`` (force a value of that kind) or
722	        # ``("m",)`` (omit the innermost field).
723	        self.recipes: list[tuple[str, tuple]] = []
724	        self._steps: list[tuple] = []
725	
726	    @contextlib.contextmanager
727	    def _step(self, step: tuple) -> Iterator[None]:
728	        self._steps.append(step)
729	        try:
730	            yield
731	        finally:
732	            self._steps.pop()
733	
734	    def witness(self, direction: str, terminal: tuple) -> None:
735	        """Record a witness recipe for one breaking pair position.
736	
737	        ``direction`` names the accepting (record) side for the breaking
738	        direction being witnessed (``"old"`` for a backward-breaking
739	        position, ``"new"`` for a forward-breaking one); ``terminal`` is
740	        the recipe's terminal step. Every call site is a non-collapsed
741	        exact branch the accepting side demonstrably accepts.
742	        """
743	        self.recipes.append((direction, tuple(self._steps) + (terminal,)))
744	
745	    def diff(self, old_root: dict, new_root: dict) -> dict:
746	        backward, forward = self.compare_object(old_root, new_root, "$")
747	        self.changes.sort(key=lambda change: (change["path"], change["change"]))
748	        return {
749	            "backward": backward,
750	            "forward": forward,
751	            "changes": self.changes,
752	            "unknown_reasons": sorted(self.reasons),
753	        }
754	
755	    def change(self, path: str, category: str, breaking: bool) -> None:
756	        self.changes.append(
757	            {"path": path, "change": category, "breaking": breaking}
758	        )
759	
760	    def compare_object(self, old: dict, new: dict, path: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
761	        if _is_collapsed(old) or _is_collapsed(new):
762	            # A depth-capped object lets anything nested through check, so
763	            # neither direction can be settled field by field.
764	            self.reasons.add(path)
765	            return _UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN
766	        verdict = _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
767	        old_fields = old["fields"]
768	        new_fields = new["fields"]
769	        old_overflow = old.get("overflow")
770	        new_overflow = new.get("overflow")
771	        for name in sorted(set(old_fields) | set(new_fields)):
772	            field_path = _join(path, name)
773	            old_entry = old_fields.get(name)
774	            new_entry = new_fields.get(name)
775	            if old_entry is not None and new_entry is not None:
776	                with self._step((_FIELD, name)):
777	                    pair = self.compare_entry(old_entry, new_entry, field_path)
778	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, pair)
779	            elif old_entry is not None:
780	                # The field disappears from the new exact fields. New check
781	                # only accepts it when the name really folded into the new
782	                # overflow entry, whose merged type set is approximate.
783	                if _overflow_routes(new_overflow, name):
784	                    self.reasons.add(_marker_path(path))
785	                    verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN))
786	                else:
787	                    # New check rejects records carrying it; old records
788	                    # omitting it additionally fail an old required field
789	                    # under the forward direction.
790	                    self.change(field_path, "field_removed", True)
791	                    with self._step((_FIELD, name)):
792	                        # A legal new record omits it; the old
793	                        # required-field check reports it missing. That
794	                        # witness needs no value kind.
795	                        if not old_entry["optional"]:
796	                            self.witness("new", (_MISSING,))
797	                        kind = self._witness_present_kind(old_entry)
798	                        if kind is not None:
799	                            # A legal old record carries the field; new
800	                            # check reports it as unexpected.
801	                            self.witness("old", (_KIND, kind))
802	                    verdict = _combine_pair(
803	                        verdict,
804	                        (_BREAKING,
805	                         _BREAKING if not old_entry["optional"] else _COMPATIBLE),
806	                    )
807	            else:
808	                # The field appears only among the new exact fields. Old
809	                # check accepts it only through its own overflow entry.
810	                if _overflow_routes(old_overflow, name):
811	                    self.reasons.add(_marker_path(path))
812	                    verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN))
813	                else:
814	                    # Backward: an old record omits it, so a new required
815	                    # field rejects that record while a new optional one
816	                    # lets it through. Forward: old check calls any record
817	                    # carrying it unexpected.
818	                    self.change(
819	                        field_path, "field_added", not new_entry["optional"]
820	                    )
821	                    with self._step((_FIELD, name)):
822	                        # A legal old record omits it; the new
823	                        # required-field check reports it missing.
824	                        if not new_entry["optional"]:
825	                            self.witness("old", (_MISSING,))
826	                        kind = self._witness_present_kind(new_entry)
827	                        if kind is not None:
828	                            # A legal new record carries the field; old
829	                            # check reports it as unexpected.
830	                            self.witness("new", (_KIND, kind))
831	                    verdict = _combine_pair(
832	                        verdict,
833	                        (_BREAKING if not new_entry["optional"] else _COMPATIBLE,
834	                         _BREAKING),
835	                    )
836	        # A live overflow entry on either side folds names whose accepted
837	        # branches cannot be attributed exactly; every branch it governs is
838	        # unknown both ways. The marker can never be a real field name.
839	        for entry in (old_overflow, new_overflow):
840	            if entry is not None and _overflow_live(entry):
841	                self.reasons.add(_marker_path(path))
842	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN))
843	        return verdict

845	    @staticmethod
846	    def _witness_present_kind(entry: dict) -> str | None:
847	        """Deterministic kind a legal record uses for this exact entry.
848	
849	        Exact field entries compared here are never approximate, and a
850	        validated entry has observed at least one record, so its type set
851	        is non-empty. The fixed kind order (null, boolean, number, string,
852	        array, object) makes the choice independent of dict iteration
853	        order; scalars are preferred and an array precedes an object.
854	        """
855	        for kind in _KINDS:
856	            if kind in entry["types"]:
857	                return kind
858	        return None
859	
860	    def compare_entry(
861	        self, old: dict, new: dict, path: str
862	    ) -> tuple[str, str]:
863	        if old.get("approximate") or new.get("approximate"):
864	            # An entry flagged approximate absorbed overflow statistics in
865	            # an exact field position; its accepted value set cannot be
866	            # attributed precisely, so no change beneath it is asserted.
867	            self.reasons.add(path)
868	            return _UNKNOWN, _UNKNOWN
869	        verdict = _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
870	        if old["optional"] != new["optional"]:
871	            if old["optional"]:
872	                # Optional becomes required: old records may omit it. The
873	                # field name is the current innermost step; the missing
874	                # witness omits exactly that field.
875	                self.change(path, "optional_to_required", True)
876	                self.witness("old", (_MISSING,))
877	                verdict = (_BREAKING, _COMPATIBLE)
878	            else:
879	                # Required becomes optional: new records may omit it.
880	                self.change(path, "required_to_optional", False)
881	                self.witness("new", (_MISSING,))
882	                verdict = (_COMPATIBLE, _BREAKING)
883	        verdict = _combine_pair(
884	            verdict, self.compare_types(old["types"], new["types"], path, "type")
885	        )
886	        return verdict

888	    def compare_types(
889	        self, old_types: dict, new_types: dict, path: str, prefix: str
890	    ) -> tuple[str, str]:
891	        verdict = _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
892	        for kind in _KINDS:
893	            if kind not in old_types and kind not in new_types:
894	                continue
895	            old_node = old_types.get(kind)
896	            new_node = new_types.get(kind)
897	            if old_node is not None and new_node is not None:
898	                verdict = _combine_pair(
899	                    verdict, self.compare_kind(old_node, new_node, path)
900	                )
901	            elif old_node is not None:
902	                # Records of this kind are legal on the old side but the
903	                # new type set no longer contains it (narrowing). A record
904	                # forcing exactly this kind is the backward witness.
905	                self.change(path, f"{prefix}_{kind}_removed", True)
906	                self.witness("old", (_KIND, kind))
907	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_BREAKING, _COMPATIBLE))
908	            else:
909	                # The new side widened with this kind; old check rejects
910	                # new records that take it (forward breaking), while old
911	                # records still pass the new, wider check.
912	                self.change(path, f"{prefix}_{kind}_added", False)
913	                self.witness("new", (_KIND, kind))
914	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_COMPATIBLE, _BREAKING))
915	        return verdict

917	    def compare_kind(
918	        self, old_node: dict, new_node: dict, path: str
919	    ) -> tuple[str, str]:
920	        kind = old_node["kind"]
921	        if kind in ("null", "boolean", "number", "string"):
922	            return _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
923	        if kind == "object":
924	            return self.compare_object(old_node, new_node, path)
925	        return self.compare_arrays(old_node, new_node, path)

927	    def compare_arrays(
928	        self, old: dict, new: dict, path: str
929	    ) -> tuple[str, str]:
930	        """Compare array element branches under one schema-level path.
931	
932	        check walks every element against the single merged element type
933	        set (a schema has no concrete indices), and it enforces that set
934	        even for a depth-capped array - only a collapsed *child* hides
935	        structure. So scalar element kinds gate exactly (rendered as
936	        ``path[]``) and collapsed element objects taint beneath them;
937	        element objects then join fields normally (``path[].name``). The
938	        matching array-level step marks the one nesting level check
939	        descends through per element.
940	        """
941	        element_path = f"{path}[]"
942	        verdict = _COMPATIBLE, _COMPATIBLE
943	        for kind in _KINDS:
944	            if kind not in old["elements"] and kind not in new["elements"]:
945	                continue
946	            old_child = old["elements"].get(kind)
947	            new_child = new["elements"].get(kind)
948	            if old_child is not None and new_child is not None:
949	                with self._step((_ARRAY,)):
950	                    pair = self.compare_kind(old_child, new_child, element_path)
951	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, pair)
952	            elif old_child is not None:
953	                self.change(element_path, f"element_type_{kind}_removed", True)
954	                with self._step((_ARRAY,)):
955	                    self.witness("old", (_KIND, kind))
956	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_BREAKING, _COMPATIBLE))
957	            else:
958	                self.change(element_path, f"element_type_{kind}_added", False)
959	                with self._step((_ARRAY,)):
960	                    self.witness("new", (_KIND, kind))
961	                verdict = _combine_pair(verdict, (_COMPATIBLE, _BREAKING))
962	        return verdict

972	# -- breaking-change witnesses ----------------------------------------------
973	#
974	# A witness for a breaking direction is one JSON object that the accepting
975	# revision's ``check`` accepts (an empty report list) and the rejecting
976	# revision's ``check`` rejects (the full, non-empty report list). The
977	# differ records one recipe per breaking pair position while it walks; a
978	# recipe is a tuple of tagged steps from the root object, and the builder
979	# below turns each into a concrete, deterministic record straight off the
980	# accepting revision's tree - it never parses change strings and never
981	# invents fields, kinds or values the accepting schema has not observed.
982	# Required sibling fields are filled along the way so the record is legal
983	# as a whole, not just at the breaking position; approximated branches are
984	# never forced (a recipe can only end on a branch the differ proved), so
985	# an ``unknown`` direction simply yields no witness.
986	
987	# Canonical, deterministic leaf values. Booleans and numbers stay
988	# distinct kinds (``True`` is never used where a number is required), and
989	# ``None`` is only produced for the explicit null kind, never for a
990	# missing field.
991	_WITNESS_VALUES = {
992	    "null": None,
993	    "boolean": True,
994	    "number": 1,
995	    "string": "x",
996	}

1000	    """Run the exact ``check`` pipeline against an in-memory root."""
1001	    reports: list[str] = []
1002	    if not isinstance(record, dict):
1003	        return [f"$: type {_kind_of(record)} not in field types [object]"]
1004	    _check_object(root, record, "$", reports)
1005	    return reports

1009	    for kind in _KINDS:
1010	        if kind in types:
1011	            return kind

1015	def _complete_value(types: dict, kind: str) -> Any:
1016	    """A deterministic value of ``kind`` legal under ``types``.
1017	
1018	    Scalars use canonical values; an object carries every required field
1019	    (each filled the same way); an array carries one complete element (or
1020	    stays empty when the schema tracked no element kinds - an empty array

1514	    tracks these limits rather than the number of records folded.
