content.content:
1	# schema-lens
2	
3	Infers a schema from a stream of JSON records and validates later records against it, so a pipeline can name and reject the records that would break its downstream consumers.
4	
5	## Requirements
6	
7	Python 3.11 or newer. Standard library only.
8	
9	## Install
10	
11	    python3 -m pip install -e .
12	
13	## Run
14	
15	    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens infer <records.jsonl>
16	    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens check <records.jsonl>
17	    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens show
18	    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens versions
19	    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens rollback <revision>
20	    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens compact [--keep <revisions>] [--background]
21	    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens status
22	    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens compat <old-revision> <new-revision>
23	    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens witness <old-revision> <new-revision>
24	    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens matrix [--revisions 1,2,3]
25	
26	`check` and `show` accept `--version <revision>` to target one specific
27	committed revision; without it they use the snapshot loaded at open time.
28	
29	## Public interface
30	
31	`schema_lens.Lens(path)` opens the lens directory `path`.
32	- `infer(records) -> dict` folds a sequence of records into the stored schema.
33	- `check(record, *, version=None) -> list[str]` reports every way one record departs from the stored schema, or from one committed revision.
34	- `schema(*, version=None) -> dict` returns the stored schema, or one committed revision.
35	- `save() -> None` and `load(*, version=None) -> None` commit and read before replacing memory.
36	- `versions() -> list[int]` lists committed revision numbers, oldest first.
37	- `rollback(version) -> int` commits the target revision's schema again as a new revision and returns the new revision number.
38	- `compact(*, keep=None, background=False) -> dict | None` merges the oldest history segment into one baseline version and returns `{"anchor": ..., "merged": [...]}` (or `None` when the history is already within the keep bound).
39	- `compaction_status() -> dict` reports the committed baseline, the revisions merged into it, the live logical history and any background run in progress.
40	- `compat(old_revision, new_revision) -> dict` reads two committed snapshots and reports how the evolution between them affects records legal under each side, without changing memory or any revision.
41	- `compat_witness(old_revision, new_revision) -> dict` returns the same report as `compat` plus a `witnesses` object with a concrete, `check`-verified counterexample for each breaking direction (`null` for compatible/unknown, both `null` on a self-comparison), without changing memory or any revision.
42	- `compat_matrix(revisions=None) -> dict` reads committed snapshots for every revision (or a strictly increasing selection) and reports both directional verdicts for every ordered pair, self-comparisons included, in one matrix.
43	- `stats() -> dict` reports fields, optional fields, observed types and observation counts.
44	- `SchemaConflict` exported exception.
45	
46	`Lens(path, max_versions=...)` (and the matching `--max-versions` command
47	line option, default 10) bounds how many complete revisions the lens
48	directory keeps; every commit beyond the bound prunes the oldest
49	revisions. A pruned revision is no longer readable or a valid rollback
50	target.
51	
52	## Revisions, snapshots and rollback
53	
54	Every `save` is one commit: the records folded since the last `load` or
55	`save` are merged into the newest committed revision and the result is
56	written as a brand new, complete, immutable revision file under
57	`versions/` (`revision-0000000001.json`, `revision-0000000002.json`, ...),
58	each carrying its own monotonic `revision` number and a SHA-256
59	`checksum` of the whole schema. Revision files are never rewritten and
60	revision numbers never repeat. A revision file appears only by an atomic
61	rename of a fully synced file, so after a crash or an interrupted commit
62	each revision is either completely readable or absent, and concurrent
63	readers always observe one complete revision or another, never a
64	half-written schema.
65	
66	Commits are serialized by `schema.lock`, a non-blocking lock file inside
67	the lens directory. When another thread or process holds the lock the
68	call raises `SchemaConflict` without changing any committed revision; the
69	in-memory batch is kept, so retrying the same `save` later lands on top of
70	everything committed in the meantime. Every revision is parsed,
71	structurally validated and checksummed in full before any of its content
72	is used. A missing or corrupt requested revision (an explicit
73	`version=`, a `rollback` target, or the newest revision on an unqualified
74	read) raises `SchemaConflict`; one damaged revision does not make the
75	other revisions unusable.
76	
77	`load()` reads the newest revision; `load(version=N)` reads exactly
78	revision N. Memory is replaced only after the read validates completely.
79	Reads while other commits are in flight are snapshots: once a lens is
80	opened at a revision, `check`/`schema`/`stats` keep answering for that
81	revision no matter how many newer commits land, until the next `load`.
82	Inference still appends batches as before; the held delta merges onto the
83	newest committed revision at the next `save`. `check(record, version=N)`
84	and `schema(version=N)` read one committed revision directly without
85	moving the open snapshot.
86	
87	`versions()` returns the committed revision numbers oldest first and is
88	empty on a directory with no history; reading any specific revision in an
89	empty history raises `SchemaConflict`. `rollback(N)` expresses the target
90	revision as a new commit: revision N is never rewritten or deleted, a new
91	revision carrying an equivalent schema is appended on top, and the
92	returned revision is what subsequent unqualified reads see. Rolling back
93	to a revision that is missing, pruned or corrupt raises `SchemaConflict`
94	and changes no committed revision.
95	
96	## Background compaction
97	
98	`compact(keep=N)` merges the oldest segment of the history into one
99	baseline version: at least the newest `N` revisions (default 5, or the
100	`compact_keep=` constructor argument / `--keep` option) stay separate and
101	every revision older than that folds into a single baseline whose schema
102	and statistics are exactly those of the last merged revision (its anchor).
103	The baseline is stored as `versions/baseline-<anchor>.json` with the same
104	checksum guarantees as a revision, and a small `versions/manifest.json` is
105	the single pointer naming it. After compaction:
106	
107	- the anchor is readable as its own revision number (via `schema`,
108	  `check`, `load` and as a `rollback` target) and answers exactly as the
109	  original anchor revision did;
110	- the other revisions merged into the baseline are no longer readable -
111	  requesting them (explicitly, by rollback, or by pinning `--version`)
112	  raises `SchemaConflict`;
113	- every surviving revision and all subsequent commits behave exactly as
114	  before; `versions()` lists the anchor followed by the surviving tail.
115	
116	Compaction never blocks a read and can run while commits land. The merge
117	reads only the files of the merged segment (the surviving tail is never
118	re-read, so one compaction round costs strictly less than re-reading the
119	whole history), builds the baseline in memory, stages it as a temp
120	artifact, and switches only after the staged tree has been checked
121	field-for-field against the anchor revision both from memory and again
122	after re-reading the staged file. The manifest pointer is replaced
123	atomically as the single switch; none of the merged revision files is
124	deleted until that replacement has landed. A crash or interruption is
125	therefore reconciled the next time the lock is taken into either "the
126	compaction fully happened" (manifest points at a complete baseline;
127	leftover merged files and stale baselines are removed) or "it never
128	happened" (no manifest; every staged baseline and temp file is removed),
129	never a half baseline or two baselines at once. While a compaction runs,
130	every read still observes one complete version through the old pointer;
131	if a commit moves the history under an in-flight compaction it retries on
132	the fresh range.
133	
134	`compact(background=True)` (or `--background`, which detaches a worker
135	process) runs the merge without blocking the caller; `compaction_status()`
136	(or the `status` command) reports whether it is `running`, its `[first,
137	last]` merged `range`, the committed `baseline` anchor and `merged`
138	revisions, the live `versions`, and any background `error`. A background
139	failure changes no committed revision and is reported there.
140	
141	Retention never deletes the baseline: the bound applies to numbered
142	revision files only, so the baseline plus the newest revisions always
143	remain readable. `compact` returns `None` (the command prints
144	`{"compacted": false}`) when the history already holds at most `keep`
145	versions.
146	
147	A lens directory that only holds the old single-file format
148	(`schema.json`, format version 1 or 2) is still read. The legacy file is
149	validated completely and migrated in place into revision 1 the first time
150	it is read (including the first explicit revision read or rollback); after
151	migration the legacy file is removed. A failed migration (say, an
152	unwritable directory) leaves the original file byte for byte untouched and
153	raises `SchemaConflict`, so the read can simply be retried later.
154	
155	The merged schema also re-imposes `max_fields` after two batches merge:
156	disjoint field names across batches can never leave a merged object node
157	holding more exact entries than the cap — excess entries fold into that
158	node's overflow entry, and with the cap in force the committed result is
159	the same schema a single capped pass over every record would produce.
160	
161	## Streaming inference under resource limits
162	
163	`infer` accepts any iterable, including a generator over a record stream,
164	and the command line reads records one at a time, so a single inference can
165	be fed millions of records in batches. Folded records are never retained:
166	once a record is folded, only the per-field and per-node statistics remain,
167	and peak memory tracks the statistics limits below rather than the number
168	of records seen.
169	
170	`Lens(path, max_fields=..., max_depth=...)` (and the matching `--max-fields`
171	/ `--max-depth` command line options) bound the statistics memory:
172	
173	- `max_fields` caps how many field entries each object node tracks
174	  exactly. Once the cap is reached, further distinct field names fold into
175	  a shared overflow entry kept under the node's `"overflow"` key and
176	  flagged `"approximate": true`.
177	- `max_depth` caps how deep object and array nodes are tracked (the root
178	  is depth 0). Deeper subtrees collapse into summary nodes flagged
179	  `"approximate": true` that keep only a record count (objects) or element
180	  type kinds (arrays).
181	
182	Both default to `None`, meaning no limit. With no limit in effect no
183	approximation is ever triggered and the folded schema is exactly the
184	schema produced by folding every record in one pass. When approximation
185	does trigger, the difference against the exact result is confined to the
186	marked entries; every unmarked field stays exact. An approximated entry's
187	type set can only widen and its observation count only grows as more
188	records are folded, so it never silently drops a type it once reported.
189	
190	Approximation is always visible, never silent: the flags appear in the
191	`schema()` tree and the `show` output, and `stats()` lists the path of
192	every approximated statistic under its `"approximate"` key — collapsed
193	subtrees by their own path, overflow entries as `$.*` under their object
194	node's path. The marker segment `*` is not a quoted key and cannot be a
195	real field name, so a field literally named `*` is still reported as
196	`$["*"]` and never confused with the overflow marker. When checking
197	records, a field name that actually folded into the overflow entry is
198	validated against its widened type set instead of being reported as
199	unexpected (the folded names are recorded in the entry's `names` list), a
200	name never seen before is still an unexpected field, and collapsed
201	subtrees are not descended into.
202	
203	## Incremental inference
204	
205	Inference is an append process: call `infer` with more batches and `save`
206	again whenever you like. Only the records folded since the last `load` or
207	`save` are merged into the committed schema, so earlier batches stay folded
208	in and are never recomputed or lost. The schema read back after any number
209	of appended batches is exactly the schema produced by folding every record
210	once in one pass; when a field cap is in force, the cap is re-imposed on
211	the merged tree after each commit so the bound holds across batches too.
212	
213	Field paths in check reports keep dotted and quoted keys apart: ordinary
214	identifier fields read as `$.user.name`, array elements as `$.tags[1]`, and
215	any key that is not an identifier is bracketed and JSON-quoted, so a field
216	literally named `a.b` is reported as `$["a.b"]` and can never be confused
217	with the nested path `$.a.b`. Backslashes are quoted the same way
218	(`$["a\\b"]`), and a field literally named `*` reads as `$["*"]`, distinct
219	from the `$.*` overflow marker.
220	
221	## Cross-revision compatibility
222	
223	`compat(old, new)` (command: `compat <old-revision> <new-revision>`) reads
224	the two complete, fully validated snapshots and reports how the evolution
225	from `old` to `new` affects records that were legal under each side. It
226	never infers, commits, rolls back or changes the open snapshot, and it
227	writes nothing but its JSON report:
228	
229	```json
230	{
231	  "from": 1,
232	  "to": 2,
233	  "backward": "compatible",
234	  "forward": "breaking",
235	  "changes": [
236	    {"path": "$.tags", "change": "element_type_number_added", "breaking": false}
237	  ],
238	  "unknown_reasons": []
239	}
240	```
241	
242	`backward` says whether the new revision accepts every record the old
243	revision accepted (can old records be read by the new schema?); `forward`
244	says whether the old revision accepts every record the new revision
245	accepts. Each verdict is one of `compatible`, `breaking` or `unknown`,
246	judged by exactly what `check` does with the record shape, field
247	optionality and the observed type sets — no defaults, enums or migrations
248	are invented.
249	
250	In the accepting direction these evolutions are non-breaking; their
251	inverses are breaking:
252	
253	- adding an *optional* field (new records may omit it; old records always
254	  do), versus removing a field (records carrying it are now unexpected);
255	- a required field becoming optional, versus an optional field becoming
256	  required (records that omitted it are now rejected);
257	- a type set widening (e.g. `number` to `number|string`), versus narrowing
258	  or a type branch disappearing, including inside nested objects and array
259	  elements.
260	
261	Objects and array elements are compared by the same rules. A schema has no
262	concrete array indices, so an element-type branch renders with `[]`
263	(`$.tags[]`) and fields of element objects join normally
264	(`$.items[].name`). `changes` lists each changed path once with its
265	category and a `breaking` flag, sorted by path then category. Field paths
266	use the same notation as `check`: ordinary identifiers as `$.name`,
267	non-identifier keys quoted as `$["a.b"]`, backslashes quoted
268	(`$["a\\b"]`), and a field literally named `*` quoted as `$["*"]`, never
269	confused with the `$.*` overflow marker.
270	
271	When an overflow entry or a depth-capped subtree on either side governs a
272	branch, the accepted values there cannot be compared exactly, so both
273	directions are `unknown` and the source is listed once in
274	`unknown_reasons` (the same paths `stats()` uses: `$.*` for an overflow
275	entry, the subtree's own path for a collapsed node). A demonstrable
276	rejection elsewhere still reports that change and settles that direction
277	as `breaking`. A revision compared with itself is `compatible` in both
278	directions with no changes, and repeating an analysis of the same pair
279	returns the same report.
280	
281	A missing, pruned/compacted-away or corrupt revision raises
282	`SchemaConflict` (the command exits `2` and prints no report); giving
283	fewer or more than two revision numbers is an argument error (`2`, no
284	report). A completed analysis exits `0` even when a verdict is `breaking`
285	or `unknown`.
286	
287	## Breaking-change witnesses
288	
289	`compat_witness(old, new)` (command: `witness <old-revision>
290	<new-revision>`) runs the same analysis as `compat` - identical fields,
291	content and ordering - and adds one `witnesses` object holding a
292	`backward` and a `forward` key. Each key is `null`, or an object with a
293	concrete counterexample:
294	
295	```json
296	{
297	  "from": 1,
298	  "to": 2,
299	  "backward": "breaking",
300	  "forward": "compatible",
301	  "changes": [
302	    {"path": "$.b", "change": "field_removed", "breaking": true}
303	  ],
304	  "unknown_reasons": [],
305	  "witnesses": {
306	    "backward": {
307	      "record": {"a": 1, "b": "x"},
308	      "reports": ["$.b: unexpected field"]
309	    },
310	    "forward": null
311	  }
312	}
313	```
314	
315	For a `backward` breaking direction, `record` is a JSON object the old
316	revision's `check` accepts (its report list is empty) and `reports` is the
317	exact, complete, non-empty list the new revision's `check` returns for it;
318	for `forward` breaking the old and new roles are swapped. Either key is
319	`null` when its direction is `compatible` or `unknown`, and a
320	self-comparison has both `null`.
321	
322	Counterexamples are assembled from the accepting revision's own schema
323	tree while the compatibility diff walks the two trees (required sibling
324	fields filled, array branches reached through a single element), and each
325	candidate is run through `check` itself before it is reported, so a
326	witness can be re-checked directly against the lens. They cover added and
327	removed fields, optionality changes, type-set changes, nested objects,
328	array element objects and multi-level arrays; booleans are never used as
329	numbers, a missing field is never represented as `null`, and an empty
330	array is used where the tracked element set admits no element. Field
331	names containing dots, backslashes or asterisks keep their real key in
332	the record while the report paths stay quoted exactly as `check` prints
333	them (`$["a.b"]`, `$["a\\b"]`, `$["*"]`). A merely approximate branch
334	yields no witness, but when another branch elsewhere proves a direction
335	breaking its witness is still supplied; only `unknown` directions have no
336	counterexample.
337	
338	The analysis is read-only - it reads and validates the two snapshots,
339	never infers, saves, rolls back, compacts or changes the open snapshot,
340	pending batches or committed history - and the same pair always produces
341	the same record, object key order, report list and command stdout bytes.
342	Invalid revision arguments (non-integers, booleans or non-positive
343	numbers) and missing, cleaned-up (pruned/compacted-away) or corrupt
344	revisions raise `SchemaConflict`; the command exits `2` with empty stdout
345	and the message on stderr, and exits `0` with only the report JSON on
346	success, including `breaking` or `unknown` conclusions.
347	
348	## Cross-version compatibility matrix
349	
350	`compat_matrix(revisions=None)` (command: `matrix [--revisions 1,2,3]`)
351	collects the pairwise reports of `compat` into one document for judging
352	upgrade and rollback risk across several revisions. It is strictly
353	read-only: it reads and validates the committed snapshots, never infers,
354	commits, rolls back, compacts, or changes the open snapshot:
355	
356	```json
357	{
358	  "revisions": [1, 2],
359	  "pairs": [
360	    {"from": 1, "to": 1, "backward": "compatible", "forward": "compatible",
361	     "changes": [], "unknown_reasons": []},
362	    {"from": 1, "to": 2, "backward": "compatible", "forward": "breaking",
363	     "changes": [{"path": "$.b", "change": "field_added", "breaking": false}],
364	     "unknown_reasons": []},
365	    {"from": 2, "to": 1, "backward": "breaking", "forward": "compatible",
366	     "changes": [{"path": "$.b", "change": "field_removed", "breaking": true}],
367	     "unknown_reasons": []},
368	    {"from": 2, "to": 2, "backward": "compatible", "forward": "compatible",
369	     "changes": [], "unknown_reasons": []}
370	  ]
371	}
372	```
373	
374	`revisions` lists the analysed revision numbers in analysis order and
375	`pairs` covers every ordered combination - including each revision
376	compared with itself - sorted by `from` then `to`. Every pair carries
377	its own `backward` and `forward` verdicts (`compatible`, `breaking` or
378	`unknown`, the two directions never merged, and `unknown` never confused
379	with another verdict), plus the same `changes` and `unknown_reasons` a
380	single `compat` report would give for that pair. A self-comparison is
381	`compatible` in both directions with empty `changes` and
382	`unknown_reasons`, even when the revision carries approximated branches;
383	pairs touching approximate fields or collapsed subtrees still report
384	fully, including their unknown reasons, and all other pairs are
385	unaffected.
386	
387	With `revisions` omitted every currently committed logical revision is
388	analysed in ascending revision order; an explicit selection must contain
389	distinct positive integers in strictly increasing order. An empty
390	history with no selection raises `SchemaConflict`; an empty selection or
391	a boolean, non-positive, duplicated or non-increasing value raises
392	`ValueError`; a revision that does not exist, has been pruned or
393	compacted away, or is corrupt raises `SchemaConflict`. The command exits
394	`2` and prints no report in every one of those cases; on success it exits
395	`0` with only the matrix JSON on stdout (errors go to stderr), and
396	repeating the same inputs produces byte-identical content and ordering.
397	
398	## Tests
399	
400	    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
401	
402	## Limits
403	
404	JSON compatible values only: no dates, decimals or binary.
405	Object fields are matched by name; array element types are merged.
406	Empty arrays contribute no element types.
407	No coercion: a record either matches the schema or is reported.
408

# schema-lens

Infers a schema from a stream of JSON records and validates later records against it, so a pipeline can name and reject the records that would break its downstream consumers.

## Requirements

Python 3.11 or newer. Standard library only.

## Install

    python3 -m pip install -e .

## Run

    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens infer <records.jsonl>
    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens check <records.jsonl>
    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens show
    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens versions
    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens rollback <revision>
    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens compact [--keep <revisions>] [--background]
    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens status
    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens compat <old-revision> <new-revision>
    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens witness <old-revision> <new-revision>
    python3 -m schema_lens --path ./lens matrix [--revisions 1,2,3]

`check` and `show` accept `--version <revision>` to target one specific
committed revision; without it they use the snapshot loaded at open time.

## Public interface

`schema_lens.Lens(path)` opens the lens directory `path`.
- `infer(records) -> dict` folds a sequence of records into the stored schema.
- `check(record, *, version=None) -> list[str]` reports every way one record departs from the stored schema, or from one committed revision.
- `schema(*, version=None) -> dict` returns the stored schema, or one committed revision.
- `save() -> None` and `load(*, version=None) -> None` commit and read before replacing memory.
- `versions() -> list[int]` lists committed revision numbers, oldest first.
- `rollback(version) -> int` commits the target revision's schema again as a new revision and returns the new revision number.
- `compact(*, keep=None, background=False) -> dict | None` merges the oldest history segment into one baseline version and returns `{"anchor": ..., "merged": [...]}` (or `None` when the history is already within the keep bound).
- `compaction_status() -> dict` reports the committed baseline, the revisions merged into it, the live logical history and any background run in progress.
- `compat(old_revision, new_revision) -> dict` reads two committed snapshots and reports how the evolution between them affects records legal under each side, without changing memory or any revision.
- `compat_witness(old_revision, new_revision) -> dict` returns the same report as `compat` plus a `witnesses` object with a concrete, `check`-verified counterexample for each breaking direction (`null` for compatible/unknown, both `null` on a self-comparison), without changing memory or any revision.
- `compat_matrix(revisions=None) -> dict` reads committed snapshots for every revision (or a strictly increasing selection) and reports both directional verdicts for every ordered pair, self-comparisons included, in one matrix.
- `stats() -> dict` reports fields, optional fields, observed types and observation counts.
- `SchemaConflict` exported exception.

`Lens(path, max_versions=...)` (and the matching `--max-versions` command
line option, default 10) bounds how many complete revisions the lens
directory keeps; every commit beyond the bound prunes the oldest
revisions. A pruned revision is no longer readable or a valid rollback
target.

## Revisions, snapshots and rollback

Every `save` is one commit: the records folded since the last `load` or
`save` are merged into the newest committed revision and the result is
written as a brand new, complete, immutable revision file under
`versions/` (`revision-0000000001.json`, `revision-0000000002.json`, ...),
each carrying its own monotonic `revision` number and a SHA-256
`checksum` of the whole schema. Revision files are never rewritten and
revision numbers never repeat. A revision file appears only by an atomic
rename of a fully synced file, so after a crash or an interrupted commit
each revision is either completely readable or absent, and concurrent
readers always observe one complete revision or another, never a
half-written schema.

Commits are serialized by `schema.lock`, a non-blocking lock file inside
the lens directory. When another thread or process holds the lock the
call raises `SchemaConflict` without changing any committed revision; the
in-memory batch is kept, so retrying the same `save` later lands on top of
everything committed in the meantime. Every revision is parsed,
structurally validated and checksummed in full before any of its content
is used. A missing or corrupt requested revision (an explicit
`version=`, a `rollback` target, or the newest revision on an unqualified
read) raises `SchemaConflict`; one damaged revision does not make the
other revisions unusable.

`load()` reads the newest revision; `load(version=N)` reads exactly
revision N. Memory is replaced only after the read validates completely.
Reads while other commits are in flight are snapshots: once a lens is
opened at a revision, `check`/`schema`/`stats` keep answering for that
revision no matter how many newer commits land, until the next `load`.
Inference still appends batches as before; the held delta merges onto the
newest committed revision at the next `save`. `check(record, version=N)`
and `schema(version=N)` read one committed revision directly without
moving the open snapshot.

`versions()` returns the committed revision numbers oldest first and is
empty on a directory with no history; reading any specific revision in an
empty history raises `SchemaConflict`. `rollback(N)` expresses the target
revision as a new commit: revision N is never rewritten or deleted, a new
revision carrying an equivalent schema is appended on top, and the
returned revision is what subsequent unqualified reads see. Rolling back
to a revision that is missing, pruned or corrupt raises `SchemaConflict`
and changes no committed revision.

## Background compaction

`compact(keep=N)` merges the oldest segment of the history into one
baseline version: at least the newest `N` revisions (default 5, or the
`compact_keep=` constructor argument / `--keep` option) stay separate and
every revision older than that folds into a single baseline whose schema
and statistics are exactly those of the last merged revision (its anchor).
The baseline is stored as `versions/baseline-<anchor>.json` with the same
checksum guarantees as a revision, and a small `versions/manifest.json` is
the single pointer naming it. After compaction:

- the anchor is readable as its own revision number (via `schema`,
  `check`, `load` and as a `rollback` target) and answers exactly as the
  original anchor revision did;
- the other revisions merged into the baseline are no longer readable -
  requesting them (explicitly, by rollback, or by pinning `--version`)
  raises `SchemaConflict`;
- every surviving revision and all subsequent commits behave exactly as
  before; `versions()` lists the anchor followed by the surviving tail.

Compaction never blocks a read and can run while commits land. The merge
reads only the files of the merged segment (the surviving tail is never
re-read, so one compaction round costs strictly less than re-reading the
whole history), builds the baseline in memory, stages it as a temp
artifact, and switches only after the staged tree has been checked
field-for-field against the anchor revision both from memory and again
after re-reading the staged file. The manifest pointer is replaced
atomically as the single switch; none of the merged revision files is
deleted until that replacement has landed. A crash or interruption is
therefore reconciled the next time the lock is taken into either "the
compaction fully happened" (manifest points at a complete baseline;
leftover merged files and stale baselines are removed) or "it never
happened" (no manifest; every staged baseline and temp file is removed),
never a half baseline or two baselines at once. While a compaction runs,
every read still observes one complete version through the old pointer;
if a commit moves the history under an in-flight compaction it retries on
the fresh range.

`compact(background=True)` (or `--background`, which detaches a worker
process) runs the merge without blocking the caller; `compaction_status()`
(or the `status` command) reports whether it is `running`, its `[first,
last]` merged `range`, the committed `baseline` anchor and `merged`
revisions, the live `versions`, and any background `error`. A background
failure changes no committed revision and is reported there.

Retention never deletes the baseline: the bound applies to numbered
revision files only, so the baseline plus the newest revisions always
remain readable. `compact` returns `None` (the command prints
`{"compacted": false}`) when the history already holds at most `keep`
versions.

A lens directory that only holds the old single-file format
(`schema.json`, format version 1 or 2) is still read. The legacy file is
validated completely and migrated in place into revision 1 the first time
it is read (including the first explicit revision read or rollback); after
migration the legacy file is removed. A failed migration (say, an
unwritable directory) leaves the original file byte for byte untouched and
raises `SchemaConflict`, so the read can simply be retried later.

The merged schema also re-imposes `max_fields` after two batches merge:
disjoint field names across batches can never leave a merged object node
holding more exact entries than the cap — excess entries fold into that
node's overflow entry, and with the cap in force the committed result is
the same schema a single capped pass over every record would produce.

## Streaming inference under resource limits

`infer` accepts any iterable, including a generator over a record stream,
and the command line reads records one at a time, so a single inference can
be fed millions of records in batches. Folded records are never retained:
once a record is folded, only the per-field and per-node statistics remain,
and peak memory tracks the statistics limits below rather than the number
of records seen.

`Lens(path, max_fields=..., max_depth=...)` (and the matching `--max-fields`
/ `--max-depth` command line options) bound the statistics memory:

- `max_fields` caps how many field entries each object node tracks
  exactly. Once the cap is reached, further distinct field names fold into
  a shared overflow entry kept under the node's `"overflow"` key and
  flagged `"approximate": true`.
- `max_depth` caps how deep object and array nodes are tracked (the root
  is depth 0). Deeper subtrees collapse into summary nodes flagged
  `"approximate": true` that keep only a record count (objects) or element
  type kinds (arrays).

Both default to `None`, meaning no limit. With no limit in effect no
approximation is ever triggered and the folded schema is exactly the
schema produced by folding every record in one pass. When approximation
does trigger, the difference against the exact result is confined to the
marked entries; every unmarked field stays exact. An approximated entry's
type set can only widen and its observation count only grows as more
records are folded, so it never silently drops a type it once reported.

Approximation is always visible, never silent: the flags appear in the

every approximated statistic under its `"approximate"` key — collapsed
subtrees by their own path, overflow entries as `$.*` under their object
node's path. The marker segment `*` is not a quoted key and cannot be a
real field name, so a field literally named `*` is still reported as
`$["*"]` and never confused with the overflow marker. When checking
records, a field name that actually folded into the overflow entry is
validated against its widened type set instead of being reported as
unexpected (the folded names are recorded in the entry's `names` list), a
name never seen before is still an unexpected field, and collapsed
subtrees are not descended into.

## Incremental inference

Inference is an append process: call `infer` with more batches and `save`
again whenever you like. Only the records folded since the last `load` or
`save` are merged into the committed schema, so earlier batches stay folded

from the `$.*` overflow marker.

  "backward": "breaking",

  "changes": [

  ],

## Cross-version compatibility matrix

`compat_matrix(revisions=None)` (command: `matrix [--revisions 1,2,3]`)

```json

  "revisions": [1, 2],
  "pairs": [
    {"from": 1, "to": 1, "backward": "compatible", "forward": "compatible",
     "changes": [], "unknown_reasons": []},
    {"from": 1, "to": 2, "backward": "compatible", "forward": "breaking",
     "changes": [{"path": "$.b", "change": "field_added", "breaking": false}],
     "unknown_reasons": []},
    {"from": 2, "to": 1, "backward": "breaking", "forward": "compatible",
     "changes": [{"path": "$.b", "change": "field_removed", "breaking": true}],
     "unknown_reasons": []},
    {"from": 2, "to": 2, "backward": "compatible", "forward": "compatible",
     "changes": [], "unknown_reasons": []}
  ]
}
```

`revisions` lists the analysed revision numbers in analysis order and
`pairs` covers every ordered combination - including each revision
compared with itself - sorted by `from` then `to`. Every pair carries
its own `backward` and `forward` verdicts (`compatible`, `breaking` or
`unknown`, the two directions never merged, and `unknown` never confused
with another verdict), plus the same `changes` and `unknown_reasons` a
single `compat` report would give for that pair. A self-comparison is
`compatible` in both directions with empty `changes` and
`unknown_reasons`, even when the revision carries approximated branches;
pairs touching approximate fields or collapsed subtrees still report
fully, including their unknown reasons, and all other pairs are
unaffected.

With `revisions` omitted every currently committed logical revision is
analysed in ascending revision order; an explicit selection must contain
distinct positive integers in strictly increasing order. An empty
history with no selection raises `SchemaConflict`; an empty selection or
a boolean, non-positive, duplicated or non-increasing value raises
`ValueError`; a revision that does not exist, has been pruned or
compacted away, or is corrupt raises `SchemaConflict`. The command exits
`2` and prints no report in every one of those cases; on success it exits
`0` with only the matrix JSON on stdout (errors go to stderr), and
repeating the same inputs produces byte-identical content and ordering.

## Tests

    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .

## Limits

JSON compatible values only: no dates, decimals or binary.
Object fields are matched by name; array element types are merged.
Empty arrays contribute no element types.
No coercion: a record either matches the schema or is reported.

import contextlib

import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import unittest
from contextlib import redirect_stdout
from pathlib import Path

from schema_lens import Lens, SchemaConflict
from schema_lens.__main__ import _read_records, main as cli_main
from schema_lens.core import (
    DEFAULT_MAX_VERSIONS,
    LOCK_FILENAME,
    OVERFLOW_MARKER,
    SCHEMA_FILENAME,
    SCHEMA_VERSION,
    VERSIONS_DIRNAME,
)
try:
    import fcntl
except ImportError:
    fcntl = None


def revision_path(directory: str, revision: int) -> Path:
    return Path(directory, VERSIONS_DIRNAME, f"revision-{revision:010d}.json")


class InferTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.dir.cleanup)
        self.lens = Lens(self.dir.name)

    def test_merges_types_of_same_named_field(self):
        schema = self.lens.infer([{"a": 1}, {"a": "x"}, {"a": 2.5}])
        entry = schema["fields"]["a"]
        self.assertEqual(sorted(entry["types"]), ["number", "string"])
        self.assertEqual(entry["observed"], 3)
        self.assertEqual(entry["total"], 3)
        self.assertFalse(entry["optional"])

    def test_field_present_in_some_records_is_optional(self):
        schema = self.lens.infer([{"a": 1, "b": "x"}, {"a": 2}])
        self.assertFalse(schema["fields"]["a"]["optional"])
        self.assertTrue(schema["fields"]["b"]["optional"])
        self.assertEqual(schema["fields"]["b"]["observed"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(schema["fields"]["b"]["total"], 2)

    def test_optionality_accumulates_across_batches(self):
        self.lens.infer([{"a": 1}])
        schema = self.lens.infer([{"b": 2}])
        self.assertTrue(schema["fields"]["a"]["optional"])
        self.assertTrue(schema["fields"]["b"]["optional"])
        self.assertEqual(schema["count"], 2)

    def test_nested_objects_merge_by_field_name(self):
        schema = self.lens.infer(
            [
                {"user": {"name": "ann", "age": 3}},
                {"user": {"name": "bob"}},
            ]
        )
        user = schema["fields"]["user"]["types"]["object"]
        self.assertEqual(user["count"], 2)
        self.assertFalse(user["fields"]["name"]["optional"])
        self.assertTrue(user["fields"]["age"]["optional"])

    def test_array_elements_merge_by_type(self):
        schema = self.lens.infer([{"tags": ["a", 1, None]}, {"tags": ["b"]}])
        elements = schema["fields"]["tags"]["types"]["array"]["elements"]
        self.assertEqual(sorted(elements), ["null", "number", "string"])

    def test_array_of_objects_merges_element_fields(self):
        schema = self.lens.infer([{"items": [{"x": 1}, {"x": 2, "y": "s"}]}])
        items = schema["fields"]["items"]["types"]["array"]["elements"]["object"]

    def test_report_shape_and_key_set(self):
        _publish(self.dir.name, [{"a": 1}], 1)

            set(report),
            {"from", "to", "backward", "forward", "changes", "unknown_reasons"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(report["from"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(report["to"], 2)

    def test_self_comparison_is_compatible_and_empty(self):
        _publish(self.dir.name, [{"a": 1}, {"a": 2}], 1)
        report = self.lens.compat(1, 1)
        self.assertEqual(report["backward"], "compatible")
        self.assertEqual(report["forward"], "compatible")

def test_corrupt_revision_raises(self):
        self._publish([{"a": 1}], 1)
        self._publish([{"a": 2}], 2)
        revision_path(self.dir.name, 2).write_text("{broken", encoding="utf-8")
        with self.assertRaises(SchemaConflict):
            self.lens.compat_witness(1, 2)

    def test_invalid_revision_arguments_raise(self):
        for bad_old, bad_new in (
            (0, 1), (1, 0), (-1, 2), (2, -1),
            (True, 1), (1, False), (1.5, 2), (1, 2.0),
            ("1", 2), (1, "2"),
        ):
            with self.assertRaises(SchemaConflict):
                self.lens.compat_witness(bad_old, bad_new)

    def test_legacy_single_file_migrates_then_witnesses(self):
        from schema_lens.core import _checksum

        root = Lens(tempfile.mkdtemp())
        root.infer([{"a": 1}])
        snapshot = root.schema()
        Path(self.dir.name, SCHEMA_FILENAME).write_text(
            json.dumps(
                {"version": 2, "checksum": _checksum(snapshot),
                 "root": snapshot},
                indent=2, sort_keys=True,
            )
            + "\n",
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
        lens = Lens(self.dir.name)
        report = lens.compat_witness(1, 1)
        self.assertEqual(report["witnesses"],
                         {"backward": None, "forward": None})


class WitnessCliTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.dir.cleanup)
        self.lens_dir = str(Path(self.dir.name, "lens"))
        self.records = str(Path(self.dir.name, "records.jsonl"))

    def _write(self, records):
        with open(self.records, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            for record in records:
                handle.write(json.dumps(record) + "\n")

    def _run(self, *argv):
        out = io.StringIO()
        err = io.StringIO()
        with redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):
            code = cli_main(list(argv))
        return code, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()

    def _commit(self, records):
        self._write(records)
        code, _, _ = self._run("--path", self.lens_dir, "infer", self.records)
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)

    def test_witness_outputs_json_report(self):
        # rev 2 drops b; a rollback republishes rev 1's exact schema as
        # rev 3, so 2 -> 3 is a clean required-field addition.
        self._commit([{"a": 1, "b": "x"}])
        self._commit([{"a": 2}])
        code, _, _ = self._run("--path", self.lens_dir, "rollback", "1")
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        code, out, err = self._run(
            "--path", self.lens_dir, "witness", "2", "3"
        )
        self.assertEqual(code, 0)
        self.assertEqual(err, "")
        report = json.loads(out)
        self.assertEqual(
            set(report),
            {"from", "to", "backward", "forward", "changes",
             "unknown_reasons", "witnesses"},
        )
        self.assertTrue(out.endswith("\n"))

class MigrateTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.dir.cleanup)
        self.lens = Lens(self.dir.name)

    def _publish(self, records, revision, **limits):
        _publish(self.dir.name, records, revision, **limits)

    def test_report_is_compat_report_plus_migration(self):
        self._publish([{"a": 1}], 1)
        self._publish([{"a": 2}], 2)
        report = self.lens.migrate({"a": 1}, 1, 2, [])
        compat = self.lens.compat(1, 2)
        self.assertEqual(set(report), set(compat) | {"migration"})
        for key in compat:
            self.assertEqual(report[key], compat[key])
        self.assertEqual(
            set(report["migration"]), {"stage", "record", "reports"}
        )

    def test_empty_rules_validate_without_transforming(self):
        self._publish([{"a": 1, "b": "x"}], 1)
        self._publish([{"a": 2, "b": "y"}], 2)
        record = {"a": 5, "b": "z"}
        report = self.lens.migrate(record, 1, 2, [])
        self.assertEqual(
            report["migration"],
            {"stage": "done", "record": {"a": 5, "b": "z"}, "reports": []},
        )
        # The returned record is a copy; the input is untouched.
        self.assertEqual(record, {"a": 5, "b": "z"})
        self.assertIsNot(report["migration"]["record"], record)

    def test_source_check_failure_reports_source_stage(self):
        self._publish([{"a": 1, "b": "x"}], 1)
        self._publish([{"a": 2, "b": "y"}], 2)
        record = {"a": 1}
        report = self.lens.migrate(record, 1, 2, [])
        self.assertEqual(report["migration"]["stage"], "source")
        self.assertIsNone(report["migration"]["record"])
        self.assertEqual(
            report["migration"]["reports"],
            self.lens.check(record, version=1),
        )
        self.assertTrue(report["migration"]["reports"])

    def test_target_check_failure_reports_target_stage(self):
        self._publish([{"a": 1, "b": "x"}], 1)
        self._publish([{"a": 2}], 2)
        record = {"a": 1, "b": "x"}
        report = self.lens.migrate(record, 1, 2, [])
        self.assertEqual(report["migration"]["stage"], "target")
        self.assertIsNone(report["migration"]["record"])
        self.assertEqual(
            report["migration"]["reports"],
            self.lens.check(record, version=2),
        )
        self.assertTrue(report["migration"]["reports"])

    def test_rename_moves_value_between_revisions(self):
        self._publish([{"name": "ann", "age": 3}], 1)
        self._publish([{"full_name": "x", "age": 1}], 2)
        rules = [{"op": "rename", "path": ["name"], "to": "full_name"}]
        report = self.lens.migrate({"name": "ann", "age": 3}, 1, 2, rules)
        self.assertEqual(report["migration"]["stage"], "done")
        self.assertEqual(
            report["migration"]["record"], {"full_name": "ann", "age": 3}
        )

    def test_rename_keeps_field_position_and_value(self):
        self._publish([{"a": 1, "b": "x", "c": True}], 1)
        rules = [{"op": "rename", "path": ["b"], "to": "d"}]
        report = self.lens.migrate({"a": 1, "b": "x", "c": False}, 1, 1, rules)
        self.assertEqual(report["migration"]["stage"], "target")
        migrated = {"a": 1, "d": "x", "c": False}
        self.assertEqual(
            report["migration"]["reports"],
            self.lens.check(migrated, version=1),
        )
        # Position is preserved under the new name on a passing record.
        self._publish([{"a": 1, "d": "x", "c": True}], 2)
        report = self.lens.migrate({"a": 1, "b": "x", "c": False}, 1, 2, rules)
        self.assertEqual(report["migration"]["stage"], "done")
        self.assertEqual(
            list(report["migration"]["record"]), ["a", "d", "c"]
        )

    def test_rename_missing_source_skips(self):
        self._publish([{"a": 1}], 1)
        rules = [{"op": "rename", "path": ["missing"], "to": "other"}]
        report = self.lens.migrate({"a": 1}, 1, 1, rules)
        self.assertEqual(
            report["migration"],
            {"stage": "done", "record": {"a": 1}, "reports": []},
        )

    def test_rename_existing_target_raises(self):
        self._publish([{"a": 1, "b": 2}], 1)
        rules = [{"op": "rename", "path": ["a"], "to": "b"}]
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.lens.migrate({"a": 1, "b": 2}, 1, 1, rules)

    def test_drop_removes_field_and_skips_missing(self):
        self._publish([{"a": 1, "b": "x"}], 1)
        self._publish([{"a": 2}], 2)
        rules = [{"op": "drop", "path": ["b"]}]
        report = self.lens.migrate({"a": 1, "b": "x"}, 1, 2, rules)
        self.assertEqual(
            report["migration"],
            {"stage": "done", "record": {"a": 1}, "reports": []},
        )
        # Dropping an absent field is a no-op.
        self._publish([{"a": 3, "c": 1}], 3)
        report = self.lens.migrate({"a": 1, "b": "x"}, 1, 1, rules)
        self.assertEqual(report["migration"]["stage"], "target")
        report = self.lens.migrate({"a": 1}, 1, 1, [{"op": "drop", "path": ["zz"]}])
        # zz is unexpected neither before nor after; the drop is skipped.
        self.assertEqual(report["migration"]["stage"], "source")

    def test_default_fills_only_missing_fields(self):
        self._publish([{"a": 1}], 1)
        self._publish([{"a": 1, "b": "x"}], 2)
        rules = [{"op": "default", "path": ["b"], "value": "x"}]
        report = self.lens.migrate({"a": 1}, 1, 2, rules)
        self.assertEqual(
            report["migration"],
            {"stage": "done", "record": {"a": 1, "b": "x"}, "reports": []},
        )

    def test_default_does_not_replace_existing_null(self):
        self._publish([{"a": 1, "b": None}], 1)
        rules = [{"op": "default", "path": ["b"], "value": "x"}]
        report = self.lens.migrate({"a": 1, "b": None}, 1, 1, rules)
        self.assertEqual(
            report["migration"],
            {"stage": "done", "record": {"a": 1, "b": None}, "reports": []},
        )

    def test_default_value_is_copied_per_application(self):
        self._publish([{"items": [{"x": 1}]}], 1)
        rules = [{"op": "default", "path": ["items", None, "y"], "value": [1]}]
        record = {"items": [{"x": 1}, {"x": 2}]}
        report = self.lens.migrate(record, 1, 1, rules)
        migrated = report["migration"]["record"]
        self.assertEqual(migrated, {"items": [{"x": 1, "y": [1]},
                                              {"x": 2, "y": [1]}]})
        self.assertIsNot(migrated["items"][0]["y"], migrated["items"][1]["y"])
        # The rule's own value object is never aliased into the result.
        self.assertIsNot(migrated["items"][0]["y"], rules[0]["value"])

    def test_rules_apply_in_order(self):
        self._publish([{"a": 1}], 1)
        self._publish([{"b": 1, "c": "x"}], 2)
        rules = [
            {"op": "rename", "path": ["a"], "to": "b"},
            {"op": "default", "path": ["c"], "value": "x"},
        ]
        report = self.lens.migrate({"a": 7}, 1, 2, rules)
        self.assertEqual(
            report["migration"],
            {"stage": "done", "record": {"b": 7, "c": "x"}, "reports": []},
        )
        # A later rule sees the earlier rule's result: drop then default
        # brings the field back with the default value.
        rules = [
            {"op": "drop", "path": ["a"]},
            {"op": "default", "path": ["a"], "value": 0},
        ]
        report = self.lens.migrate({"a": 7}, 1, 1, rules)
        self.assertEqual(report["migration"]["record"], {"a": 0})

    def test_null_segment_iterates_array_elements(self):
        self._publish([{"items": [{"a.b": 1}]}], 1)
        self._publish([{"items": [{"c": 2}]}], 2)
        rules = [{"op": "rename", "path": ["items", None, "a.b"], "to": "c"}]
        record = {"items": [{"a.b": 1}, {"a.b": 2}]}
        report = self.lens.migrate(record, 1, 2, rules)
        self.assertEqual(report["migration"]["stage"], "done")
        self.assertEqual(
            report["migration"]["record"], {"items": [{"c": 1}, {"c": 2}]}

    def test_missing_parent_skips_without_creating(self):
        self._publish([{"a": 1}], 1)
        rules = [{"op": "default", "path": ["missing", "x"], "value": 1}]
        report = self.lens.migrate({"a": 1}, 1, 1, rules)
        self.assertEqual(
            report["migration"],
            {"stage": "done", "record": {"a": 1}, "reports": []},
        )

        self._publish([{"a": 1}], 1)
        # A string segment met by a non-object.
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.lens.migrate({"a": 1}, 1, 1,

class MigrateTests(unittest.TestCase):

        self.lens = Lens(self.dir.name)

    def _publish(self, records, revision, **limits):
        _publish(self.dir.name, records, revision, **limits)

    def test_report_is_compat_report_plus_migration(self):
        self._publish([{"a": 1}], 1)
        self._publish([{"a": 2}], 2)
        report = self.lens.migrate({"a": 1}, 1, 2, [])
        compat = self.lens.compat(1, 2)
        self.assertEqual(set(report), set(compat) | {"migration"})
        for key in compat:
            self.assertEqual(report[key], compat[key])
        self.assertEqual(
            set(report["migration"]), {"stage", "record", "reports"}
        )

    def test_empty_rules_validate_without_transforming(self):
        self._publish([{"a": 1, "b": "x"}], 1)
        self._publish([{"a": 2, "b": "y"}], 2)
        record = {"a": 5, "b": "z"}
        report = self.lens.migrate(record, 1, 2, [])
        self.assertEqual(
            report["migration"],
            {"stage": "done", "record": {"a": 5, "b": "z"}, "reports": []},
        )
        # The returned record is a copy; the input is untouched.
        self.assertEqual(record, {"a": 5, "b": "z"})
        self.assertIsNot(report["migration"]["record"], record)

    def test_source_check_failure_reports_source_stage(self):
        self._publish([{"a": 1, "b": "x"}], 1)
        self._publish([{"a": 2, "b": "y"}], 2)
        record = {"a": 1}
        report = self.lens.migrate(record, 1, 2, [])
        self.assertEqual(report["migration"]["stage"], "source")
        self.assertIsNone(report["migration"]["record"])
        self.assertEqual(
            report["migration"]["reports"],
            self.lens.check(record, version=1),
        )
        self.assertTrue(report["migration"]["reports"])

    def test_target_check_failure_reports_target_stage(self):
        self._publish([{"a": 1, "b": "x"}], 1)
        self._publish([{"a": 2}], 2)
        record = {"a": 1, "b": "x"}
        report = self.lens.migrate(record, 1, 2, [])
        self.assertEqual(report["migration"]["stage"], "target")
        self.assertIsNone(report["migration"]["record"])
        self.assertEqual(
            report["migration"]["reports"],
            self.lens.check(record, version=2),
        )
        self.assertTrue(report["migration"]["reports"])

        self._publish([{"full_name": "x", "age": 1}], 2)
        rules = [{"op": "rename", "path": ["name"], "to": "full_name"}]
        report = self.lens.migrate({"name": "ann", "age": 3}, 1, 2, rules)

With `revisions` omitted every currently committed logical revision is
analysed in ascending revision order; an explicit selection must contain
distinct positive integers in strictly increasing order. An empty
history with no selection raises `SchemaConflict`; an empty selection or
a boolean, non-positive, duplicated or non-increasing value raises
`ValueError`; a revision that does not exist, has been pruned or
compacted away, or is corrupt raises `SchemaConflict`. The command exits
`2` and prints no report in every one of those cases; on success it exits
`0` with only the matrix JSON on stdout (errors go to stderr), and
repeating the same inputs produces byte-identical content and ordering.

## Explicit field migration previews

`migrate(record, old_revision, new_revision, rules)` (Python only)
combines the `compat` report for a revision pair with a concrete preview
of migrating one record between them. It reads and validates the two
committed snapshots exactly like `compat` - same read-only guarantees,
same self-comparison shortcut - and appends one `migration` object:

```json
{
  "from": 1,
  "to": 2,
  "backward": "breaking",
  "forward": "breaking",
  "changes": [
    {"path": "$.full_name", "change": "field_added", "breaking": true},
    {"path": "$.name", "change": "field_removed", "breaking": true}
  ],
  "unknown_reasons": [],
  "migration": {
    "stage": "done",
    "record": {"full_name": "ann", "age": 3},
    "reports": []
  }
}
```

The preview checks `record` against the old revision, applies the rules
in order to a copy of it (each rule sees the result of the previous
one), and checks the migrated record against the new revision - every
acceptance question is answered by `check` itself, so optional fields,
type unions and approximate branches behave exactly as
`check(record, version=...)` does. On success `stage` is `"done"`,
`record` is the complete migrated record and `reports` is empty. When
the source record fails the old revision's check the stage is
`"source"`; when the migrated record fails the new revision's check it
is `"target"`; in both cases `record` is `null` and `reports` is exactly
the list that revision's `check` returns. A same-revision migration
still applies the rules and runs both checks.

`rules` is a JSON array (an empty array validates without transforming);
each rule is an object with `op` and `path` and nothing beyond its op's
own keys:

- `{"op": "rename", "path": [...], "to": "new_name"}` renames the field
  within its object, keeping the value and the field's position; a
  missing source field skips the rule, an already present target raises
  `ValueError`, and a `to` equal to the source name is rejected up front.
- `{"op": "drop", "path": [...]}` removes the field; a missing field
  skips the rule.
- `{"op": "default", "path": [...], "value": ...}` fills the field only
  when it is missing; a present field is kept, even when it is `null`.

A path is a non-empty array whose string segments are literal field
names (dots included) and whose `null` segments iterate every element of
the array at that position; the last segment must be a string, so
`["items", null, "a.b"]` names the field literally called `a.b` inside
each element of `items`. A missing parent field skips the rule without
creating parents; a string segment met by a non-object or a `null`
segment met by a non-array raises `ValueError`; an empty array changes
nothing.

`record` must be a JSON object. A non-JSON value (in the record or in a
default), a malformed rule, an unknown op, extra or missing rule keys
and an invalid path all raise `ValueError`. Invalid revision numbers and
missing, pruned/compacted-away or corrupt revisions raise
`SchemaConflict` (a compaction anchor stays usable), and reading
revisions keeps the legacy single-file migration semantics. Beyond that
the preview writes nothing and never changes the record, the rules, the
open snapshot, pending batches or any committed revision; the same
inputs always return the same content and ordering.

完成。全部 300 个测试通过（含新增的 24 个 migrate 测试），仅修改三个文件，未触碰 CLI 与既有入口。

## 实现内容

**`schema_lens/core.py`**
- 新增 `Lens.migrate(record, old_revision, new_revision, rules)`（位于 `compat_matrix` 之后）：先按 `compat` 的同样方式校验版本号并读取两个已提交快照（`SchemaConflict` 语义、压缩锚点、旧格式迁移全部沿用），返回 compat 报告外加一个 `migration` 对象。同版本时 compat 部分走既有的自比较捷径，但规则与两次校验仍照常执行。
- 迁移流水线 `_migration_preview`：先用 `_check_against` 对源记录跑旧版本的 check（失败则 `stage="source"`、`record=None`、`reports` 为该版本 check 的完整列表）；再对深拷贝按顺序应用规则；最后对结果跑新版本 check（失败则 `stage="target"`），全部通过则 `stage="done"`、`record` 为完整迁移结果、`reports=[]`。
- 规则校验 `_validate_rule`/`_validate_rules`：rules 必须是 JSON 数组；op 只认 `rename`/`drop`/`default`；键集合必须精确匹配（额外键、缺键均 `ValueError`）；path 为非空数组、段只能是字符串或 null、末段必须是字符串；`rename` 的 `to` 必须是字符串且与源名不同；`default` 的 `value` 及整个 record 经 `_require_json_value` 递归校验（非 JSON 值、非字符串键 → `ValueError`）。校验后返回规范化副本，输入 rules 不被改动。
- 规则应用 `_apply_rule_at`/`_apply_leaf`：字符串段遇非对象、null 段遇非数组 → `ValueError`；缺失父字段跳过且不创建父对象；空数组下 null 段不产生修改；rename 保留值并保持字段在原位置改名（源缺失跳过、目标已存在抛 `ValueError`）；drop 缺失跳过；default 只补缺失字段、不替换已有 null，且每次插入都深拷贝 value（数组多元素各自独立）。

**`tests/test_schema_lens.py`** — 新增 `MigrateTests`：报告形状、三阶段语义、rename/drop/default 各自行为与跳过规则、null 段遍历、逐元素跳过、容器类型不匹配、规则顺序、同版本迁移、非法 record/rules/版本号的异常类型、损坏与缺失版本、压缩锚点、旧格式迁移、确定性与无副作用（输入记录、rules、打开的快照、待提交批次、历史均不变）。

**`README.md`** — 公共接口列表新增 `migrate` 条目，并新增 "Explicit field migration previews" 一节。

一个值得注意的设计点：源记录先校验再应用规则，所以"规则路径遇到错误容器类型"的 `ValueError` 只会在记录本身通过源校验后触发（例如字段是 number/object 类型联合、记录取了 number 分支时）——这与规格中"先校验源记录，再按顺序应用规则"的顺序一致。
